academic.childMeaning: To do with study and learning, especially at a high level.
practiceSentences: The journal publishes academic writing about art.
What academic evidence supports this reading?
Academic writing states its sources for everything.

acceleration.childMeaning: How quickly something's speed is changing.
practiceSentences: A sprinter's acceleration matters more than her top speed.
What causes the acceleration at the start of a race?
Acceleration is a change in speed, not speed itself.
The car's acceleration was measured over ten metres.

acceptable.childMeaning: Good enough to be allowed or agreed to.
practiceSentences: A draw was an acceptable result away from home.
Is that an acceptable excuse for missing training?
An acceptable standard is a floor, not a target.
The referee ruled the boots acceptable.
What is acceptable in practice may not be in a match.

accessible.childMeaning: Able to be reached, entered or understood by everyone.
practiceSentences: The site is accessible to readers using a screen reader.
Is this explanation accessible to a younger audience?
An accessible design is not a simplified one.
Captions make a video accessible to more people.
Accessible means everyone can get to it, in every sense.

accommodate.childMeaning: To make room for someone, or to change a plan to suit them.
practiceSentences: The hall can accommodate the whole of Year 6 at once.
How many readers can this library accommodate?

A good plan can accommodate one surprise without collapsing.
Accommodate is spelled with two c's and two m's.

accommodation.childMeaning: A place for someone to stay or live.
practiceSentences: The school arranged accommodation for the visiting choir.
What accommodation is there near the coast?

Finding accommodation was harder than finding the money.

Accountability means somebody can be asked to explain.
Who carries accountability when a scheme fails?
Accountability without power to act is unfair.
The new rules improved accountability for public money.

What achievement are you proudest of this year?
An achievement is measured against where you began.
The co-operative's greatest achievement was surviving its first year.
Achievement keeps the e of achieve before the ending.

acknowledgement.childMeaning: A statement accepting that something is true or has been received.
practiceSentences: The bank sent an acknowledgement of the payment.
Did you receive an acknowledgement of the order?
An acknowledgement is not the same as an agreement.
Her report opened with an acknowledgement of the help she had.
Acknowledgement keeps the e of acknowledge in British spelling.
You acquire a vocabulary by meeting words many times.
What skills did you acquire this year?
To acquire a language takes longer than to learn a list.
The library acquired the whole collection in one gift.
Acquire keeps a silent c that nobody pronounces.

adaptability.childMeaning: The ability to change to suit new conditions.
practiceSentences: Adaptability matters more than strength on a changing pitch.
What adaptability does a new sport demand?
Adaptability is a skill that can be practised.
The team's adaptability won them the second half.
Adaptability is not the same as having no plan.

adaptable.childMeaning: Able to change easily to suit a new situation.
practiceSentences: An adaptable player can cover two positions.
How adaptable is this training plan?
Adaptable equipment suits players of every size.
The coach wanted an adaptable squad, not eleven specialists.
Adaptable describes the person; adaptability is the quality.

adjacent.childMeaning: Next to or beside something else.
practiceSentences: The reserve is adjacent to the farmland.
Which habitat is adjacent to the wetland?
Two adjacent fields can hold quite different species.
Animals move between adjacent habitats through the corridor.
Adjacent means touching, or very nearly.

practiceSentences: Adjust the strap until the frame sits level.
What would you adjust first?
Adjust one thing at a time or you will not know what helped.
He adjusted the timing and the motor ran smoothly.
To adjust is to change a little; to redesign is to start again.
adjust.childMeaning: To change something slightly so it fits.

admittedly.childMeaning: Used to accept a point before making your own.

advantageous.childMeaning: Giving a benefit or putting you in a better position.

Is an early payment advantageous to the seller?

The position by the road was advantageous for trade.
Advantageous is the adjective of advantage.

advertisement.childMeaning: A notice or message made to persuade people to buy or support something.

advocacy.childMeaning: Speaking or arguing publicly in support of a cause.

Advocacy is patient work with very few quick victories.
The group's advocacy won safer crossings for the school.
Advocacy speaks for a cause; mediation speaks for neither side.

agriculture.childMeaning: The growing of crops and the raising of animals for food.
practiceSentences: Agriculture depends on rain that arrives on time.

Agriculture feeds a country before it earns for it.
New methods raised what agriculture could produce from one field.
Agriculture is farming, described from a distance.

allegory.childMeaning: A story whose characters and events stand for something larger.
practiceSentences: The fable is an allegory about greed.
What is this allegory really describing?
An allegory works on two levels at once.
Every character in the allegory stands for a kind of person.
An allegory says one thing and means another, on purpose.

alliance.childMeaning: An agreement between groups to work together for a shared purpose.

What alliance would strengthen this campaign?
An alliance lasts while the shared interest lasts.
The alliance collapsed when one side broke the terms.
An alliance is between equals; an empire is not.

Can you suggest an alternative ending for the story we read today?

amateur.childMeaning: Doing something for love of it rather than for pay.
amateur.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

amplitude.childMeaning: The height of a wave from its middle to its peak.

What analogy would make this idea clearer?
An analogy helps until it is pushed too far.

A good analogy compares the unfamiliar with the familiar.

annotate.childMeaning: To add notes to a text explaining or commenting on it.
practiceSentences: Annotate the passage before you write about it.
How would you annotate this diagram?
To annotate is to think on the page.
She annotated every source in the margin.
Annotate the argument, not just the difficult words.

annotation.childMeaning: A note added to a text to explain or comment on it.
practiceSentences: Her annotation explained why the figure was doubtful.
What annotation would help a reader here?
An annotation belongs beside the claim it questions.
The margin was full of annotations by the second reading.
An annotation comments; a citation credits.

antibody.childMeaning: A protein the body makes to attack a particular germ.
practiceSentences: The body makes an antibody shaped to fit one germ.
How long does an antibody stay in the blood?
An antibody remembers a germ it has met before.
A vaccine teaches the body to make the antibody early.
Each antibody works on one invader and no other.

arc.childMeaning: A curved part of the edge of a circle.
practiceSentences: The compass drew a neat arc across the page.
How long is this arc?
An arc is part of a circle's circumference.
The ball travelled in a high arc over the wall.
An arc is curved; a chord is the straight line across it.

arguably.childMeaning: Used to say something can be argued, though others may disagree.
practiceSentences: This is arguably the finest fable in the collection.
Is the second ending arguably the stronger one?
Arguably, the villagers are more at fault than the boy.
The opening is arguably too slow for a short tale.
Arguably signals a claim you are prepared to defend.

argumentation.childMeaning: The building of a case out of reasons and evidence.
practiceSentences: Careful argumentation matters more than a loud voice.
What makes argumentation persuasive rather than merely long?
Good argumentation answers the strongest objection, not the weakest.
Her argumentation moved from evidence to conclusion in three steps.
Argumentation is the method; an argument is one instance of it.

articulate.childMeaning: To put thoughts into clear words.
articulate.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

ascending.childMeaning: Going up, or arranged from smallest to largest.
practiceSentences: Put the measurements in ascending order.
Which list is in ascending order?
Ascending order starts with the smallest value.
The path was ascending steadily for an hour.
Ascending goes up; descending goes down.

assertion.note: Sentence 2 ran to 115 characters against this grade's cap of 108 - measured from Grade 6's own existing sentences, whose longest is 108.
practiceSentences: Support every assertion in your report with a fact, a figure, or a named source.
The article's boldest assertion demanded far stronger supporting data.

I have learnt to treat every confident assertion in advertising as a question needing proof.

assertiveness.childMeaning: Saying what you need or think clearly and without aggression.
practiceSentences: Assertiveness is saying no without an apology.
How is assertiveness different from rudeness?
Assertiveness states a need; aggression makes a demand.
She answered with quiet assertiveness and the room listened.
Assertiveness can be learned, which is why it is taught.

attached.childMeaning: Joined or fixed to something, or fond of someone.

Which document is attached to this letter?

The story felt authentic because the details were exact.
Authentic means genuinely what it claims to be.

autonomy.childMeaning: The freedom to make your own decisions.
practiceSentences: The club was given autonomy over its own budget.
How much autonomy should a class have?
Autonomy brings responsibility with it, always.
Their autonomy ended where the school's rules began.
Autonomy is self-government, whether of a person or a region.

awareness.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Awareness means knowing about...' - restating its own headword.
practiceSentences: The campaign raised awareness of safe cycling.
What awareness does a goalkeeper need of the whole pitch?
Awareness of a risk is the first step to avoiding it.
Her awareness of the rules saved the team a penalty.
Awareness is noticing; action is what follows.

awkward.childMeaning: Uncomfortable or a little difficult, especially with other people.
awkward.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Awkward means uncomfortable...' - restating the headword the learner is already looking at.
practiceSentences: There was an awkward silence after the whistle.
Was the question awkward or simply unexpected?

Awkward is an awkward word to spell.
A balanced report gives both sides their strongest case.
Is this article balanced, or does it favour one view?
She wrote a balanced conclusion instead of a verdict.
A balanced argument is not the same as a weak one.
Amal kept her speech balanced even where she disagreed.

bandwidth.childMeaning: How much data a connection can carry in a given time.
practiceSentences: Video uses far more bandwidth than text.
How much bandwidth does the school have?
Bandwidth is shared, so everyone slows down together.
Low bandwidth is why the picture keeps freezing.
Bandwidth also means how much attention a person can spare.

banking.childMeaning: The business of keeping, lending and moving people's money.
practiceSentences: Mobile banking reached the village before the road did.
How has banking changed in your grandparents' lifetime?
Banking runs on trust more than on buildings.
She works in banking and explains interest very clearly.
Banking lends out the money it is looking after.

bargain.childMeaning: Something bought cheaply, or an agreement about a price.
practiceSentences: The old bicycle was a real bargain.
Is that a bargain or just a low price?
They struck a bargain over the cost of the kit.
A bargain you never use has cost you everything.
Amara drove a hard bargain at the market.

belonging.childMeaning: The feeling of being accepted and welcome in a group.
belonging.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Belonging is the comfortable feeling...' - restating its own headword.
practiceSentences: A sense of belonging keeps players coming back.
What gives a new pupil a feeling of belonging?
Belonging comes from being needed, not just admitted.
She found a sense of belonging in the athletics club.
Belonging is built in small welcomes rather than one big one.

bias.note: Sentence 3 named Theo, who belongs to Grades 2 and 3 - the SIXTH Theo found in inherited content - and the set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: Amal worried that bias, not evidence, had shaped the officer's decision.
Could bias explain why some vendors are checked more than others?
Bias is not always deliberate, and that is what makes it hard to see.
A fair trial must never be influenced by bias of any kind.
Every source has a bias; the question is whether it is declared.

binary.childMeaning: A way of writing numbers using only 0 and 1.
practiceSentences: A computer stores everything as binary.
What is the number five in binary?
Binary uses two digits where we use ten.
Each binary digit is called a bit.
Binary is a choice between two states, on or off.

biodiversity.childMeaning: The range of different living things found in one place.
biodiversity.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Biodiversity is the wide variety...' - restating the headword the learner is already looking at.
practiceSentences: The wetland has greater biodiversity than the farmland beside it.
Why does biodiversity matter to a forest's survival?
Biodiversity protects a habitat the way variety protects a diet.
Clearing one hedge lowered the biodiversity of the whole field.
Biodiversity counts kinds of life, not numbers of animals.

bisect.childMeaning: To cut something into two equal parts.
practiceSentences: The line bisects the angle exactly.
Which line bisects this shape?
To bisect is to halve, not merely to divide.
A diagonal bisects a square into two triangles.
Bisect means cut in two; trisect means cut in three.

browser-based.childMeaning: Running inside a web browser rather than installed on the machine.
practiceSentences: The whole tool is browser-based, so nothing is installed.
Is this browser-based or does it need downloading?
A browser-based program updates for everyone at once.
Browser-based tools work on any machine with a browser.
Browser-based means the browser is doing the running.

bruise.childMeaning: A dark mark on the skin where it has been struck.
practiceSentences: A bruise appeared on his shin after the match.
How long does a bruise take to fade?
Ice reduces the swelling around a bruise.
A bruise is blood trapped under the skin.
Bruise rhymes with news, not with rise.

cache.childMeaning: A store of recently used data, kept close by so it can be fetched fast.
cache.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'A hidden store of things, often used to keep items safe' - the buried-treasure sense, on a card between networking and cursor. In computing a cache is not hidden and is not for safekeeping: it is a copy kept nearby for speed, which is the opposite emphasis.
practiceSentences: The browser keeps a cache so the page loads faster next time.
Why does clearing the cache sometimes fix a page?
A cache trades a little memory for a lot of speed.
A stale cache shows you yesterday's version of a page.
Cache is pronounced like cash, not like cachet.

capability.childMeaning: The power or skill to do something.
practiceSentences: The school now has the capability to print its own magazine.
What capability does this project still need?
A capability unused is the same as one you do not have.
Their capability grew with every year of practice.
Capability is what you could do; capacity is how much.

catalyst.childMeaning: Something that speeds up a change without being used up itself.
practiceSentences: A catalyst speeds the reaction and survives it.
Which catalyst does this process need?
An enzyme is the body's own kind of catalyst.
Without a catalyst the change would take days.
A catalyst is also a person who makes something happen.

census.childMeaning: An official count of everybody living in a country.

What does the census ask about?
A census plans the schools a district will need.

A census counts everyone; a sample counts a few.

Is there any certainty in a long-range forecast?

She spoke with a certainty the figures did not support.
Certainty is a feeling; proof is a standard.
certainty.childMeaning: Being sure that something is true.
certainty.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

chain.childMeaning: A series of things where each is linked to the next.
chain.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

challenge.childMeaning: Something difficult that tests you, or an invitation to prove a claim.

chromosome.childMeaning: A thread inside a cell that carries the genes.

Chromosome means coloured body, from the dye that first revealed it.

chronology.childMeaning: The order in which events actually happened.
practiceSentences: The chronology of the tale is not the order it is told in.
What chronology do these events really follow?

A recount follows chronology; a mystery often does not.
Chronology and plot are two different things.
The advertisement makes a claim it cannot support.
What claim is this article actually making?
A claim without evidence is only an opinion in a loud voice.
She separated the claims from the facts in two columns.
To claim is to assert; to prove is another matter.

classification.childMeaning: The sorting of things into groups by what they have in common.
practiceSentences: Job classification decides which rules apply to a worker.
What classification does this role fall under?
A classification is useful only if the groups do not overlap.
The library's classification puts every book in one place.
Classification asks what things share, not what they are called.

cloud-based.childMeaning: Stored and run on distant servers rather than on your own device.
practiceSentences: Their cloud-based storage keeps a copy off the premises.
Is a cloud-based system safer than a local one?
A cloud-based service works from any device you sign in on.
Cloud-based files survive a broken laptop.
Cloud-based means somebody else's computer, somewhere else.

coding.childMeaning: Writing the instructions that tell a computer what to do.
practiceSentences: Coding is a way of thinking before it is a way of typing.
What language did you start coding in?
Coding rewards somebody who enjoys being wrong quickly.
The club meets on Thursdays for coding.
Coding is the writing; the program is the result.

coefficient.childMeaning: The number placed in front of a letter in algebra.
practiceSentences: In 5x the coefficient is five.
What is the coefficient of y here?
A coefficient multiplies the letter it stands before.
She collected the terms and added their coefficients.
A coefficient of one is usually not written at all.

coherent.childMeaning: Clear and logical, so the parts follow one another.
coherent.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

cohesion.childMeaning: The quality of a text whose parts hold together.
practiceSentences: Linking words give a paragraph its cohesion.
What gives this article its cohesion?
Cohesion is how it holds together; coherence is whether it makes sense.
The draft lost its cohesion when two paragraphs were swapped.
Cohesion can be added; coherence has to be thought.

collaboration.childMeaning: Working together with others towards a shared goal.
collaboration.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Collaboration is the act of working together...' - restating its own headword.

Collaboration needs clear roles more than it needs goodwill.
Their collaboration produced something neither could have made alone.
Collaboration shares the work and the credit.

commence.childMeaning: To begin, especially something formal or planned.

When does the competition commence?

Commence is the formal word; begin does the same work.

commodity.note: The inherited set held four sentences, not five.

Poor communication caused the whole delay.

Communication runs both ways or it is an announcement.

compatible.childMeaning: Able to work or exist together without conflict.

Are these two accounts compatible?
Two compatible claims can both be true at once.
She looked for a compatible file format.
Compatible means they fit together, not that they are the same.

comprehensive.childMeaning: Covering everything that is relevant, leaving nothing out.
practiceSentences: The report gave a comprehensive account of every cost.
Is this a comprehensive list or a selection?
A comprehensive answer takes longer and is worth it.
She made a comprehensive survey of every stall in the market.
Comprehensive means complete; comprehensible means understandable.

conceptualise.childMeaning: To form a clear idea of something in your mind.

conductor.childMeaning: A material that lets heat or electricity pass through it.

confidential.childMeaning: Meant to be kept private and shown only to certain people.

congruent.childMeaning: Exactly the same in shape and size.

connective.childMeaning: A word that joins ideas and shows how they relate.

A connective joins ideas; a conjunction joins clauses.

contradictory.childMeaning: Saying the opposite of something else, so both cannot be true.

Two contradictory rules cannot both be followed.

controversy.childMeaning: A public disagreement in which people take strong opposite sides.
practiceSentences: The referee's decision caused a controversy that lasted weeks.
Why is there such controversy about the new rule?
A controversy is not settled by the loudest voice.
The controversy over the stadium divided the whole town.
Controversy needs two sides who both believe they are right.

cookie.childMeaning: A small file a website stores on your device to remember you.
practiceSentences: A cookie remembers that you are already signed in.
Why does this site ask about cookies?
A cookie can also record which pages you visited.
She cleared the cookies and had to sign in again.
A cookie is a file, not the biscuit.

coordinates.childMeaning: A pair of numbers giving an exact position on a grid.
practiceSentences: The coordinates place the well at the field's corner.
What are the coordinates of this point?
Coordinates name one spot and no other.
She read the coordinates from the map's edges.
Coordinates go across first, then up.

coping.childMeaning: Dealing with something difficult without being overwhelmed.
practiceSentences: Coping with a loss takes longer than people expect.
What coping strategies help before a big match?
Coping is not the same as pretending nothing is wrong.
She has her own way of coping with a noisy house.
Asking for help is a form of coping, not a failure of it.

copyright.note: Three of the five sentences were the same sentence: 'Because of copyright, an author's stories cannot be reprinted without her clear permission.', 'The author holds the copyright, so nobody may reprint her book without permission.' and 'The young artist holds the copyright to her drawings, so nobody may copy them without permission.' One idea, three times, on one card - the worst echo found in either grade.
practiceSentences: The author holds the copyright, so nobody may reprint her book without permission.
Why does copyright matter to musicians who depend on their songs for an income?
Copyright expires, and the work then belongs to everyone.
Copyright protects the expression, not the idea behind it.
I learned that copyright protects artists so others cannot steal their creative ideas.

corporation.childMeaning: A large company that the law treats as a single body.
practiceSentences: The corporation employs people in nine countries.
Which corporation owns the factory now?
A corporation outlives the people who founded it.
A corporation can be sued in its own name.
A corporation is one company; a co-operative is many owners.

correspondingly.childMeaning: In a way that matches a change just described.
practiceSentences: The pitch was longer, and the match correspondingly slower.
Did the harder training bring a correspondingly better result?
Prices rose, and attendance fell correspondingly.
Correspondingly fewer injuries followed the new warm-up.
Correspondingly signals that two changes move together.

creator.childMeaning: The person who makes or invents something.
practiceSentences: The creator of the design never patented it.
Who was the creator of this map?
A creator is remembered for one thing and forgets the rest.
She is the creator of the school's weather station.
Creator takes -or, not -er.

credible.childMeaning: Believable, because there is good reason to accept it.
credible.note: The inherited meaning was 'believable or trustworthy; something that can be trusted' - lowercase, no full stop, and circular, since it explains `trustworthy` with `can be trusted`.
practiceSentences: The witness gave a credible account of the evening.
Is that a credible explanation for the missing key?
A credible source names where its facts came from.
The excuse was not credible, and everyone knew it.
Credible means worth believing, not merely possible.

crime.childMeaning: An act that the law forbids and punishes.
practiceSentences: Reporting a crime is the first step to solving it.
What makes an act a crime rather than a mistake?
A crime is defined by law, and laws differ between countries.
The town's crime rate fell after the lighting improved.
A crime harms a person and also the public order.

critique.childMeaning: A careful judgement of a piece of work, saying what does and does not succeed.
practiceSentences: Her critique of the poem was fair and detailed.
What critique would you offer the writer?
A critique is not an attack, and not praise either.
He wrote a short critique of the article for the newsletter.
A useful critique names one thing to change first.
Curiosity is what keeps a field biologist watching for hours.
What first stirred your curiosity about wild animals?
Curiosity killed the cat, but it also wrote every field guide.
Her curiosity about the nest cost her a whole afternoon.
Curiosity asks the question; patience answers it.

current.childMeaning: A flow of electricity, water or air in one direction.
current.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'Happening or existing right now, in the present time' - the TIME sense, on a card sitting between conductor and fuel. All four of its sentences were about prices and rules, and one named Omar, Grade 3's shopkeeper. The card holds only four sentences besides. In this unit a current is what flows.
practiceSentences: An electric current flows from one terminal to the other.
How strong is the current in this river?
A current needs a complete circuit to flow at all.
The ocean current carries warm water north.
Current also means happening now, which is a different word entirely.

cursor.childMeaning: The mark on a screen showing where the next action will happen.
practiceSentences: The cursor blinks where the next letter will appear.
Where is the cursor now?
A cursor changes shape to say what a click will do.
She moved the cursor to the end of the line.
The cursor was named after a sliding part of a slide rule.

cyberbullying.childMeaning: Using messages or posts online to hurt or frighten somebody.
practiceSentences: Cyberbullying follows a person home, which is what makes it different.
What should you do if you witness cyberbullying?
Cyberbullying leaves a record, and that record can help.
The school's policy treats cyberbullying as seriously as any bullying.
Cyberbullying is not an argument; it is repeated and one-sided.

dataset.childMeaning: A collection of related information gathered for study.
practiceSentences: The dataset holds ten years of rainfall readings.
How large is this dataset?
A dataset is only as good as how it was collected.
She cleaned the dataset before drawing any chart.
A dataset can be honest and still be misleading.

debugging.childMeaning: Finding and fixing the mistakes in a program.
practiceSentences: Debugging takes longer than writing the code did.
Where would you start debugging this?
Debugging is easier if you change one thing at a time.
She spent the whole afternoon debugging a single line.
The word debugging comes from a real moth in a real machine.

decision-making.childMeaning: The process of choosing between possible courses of action.
practiceSentences: Good decision-making needs information and a deadline.
Who is responsible for decision-making here?
Decision-making improves when the options are written down.
The group's decision-making slowed as it grew.
Decision-making is a skill, not a personality.

decisive.childMeaning: Settling something firmly, or able to decide quickly.
practiceSentences: The final scene is decisive; everything before it is preparation.
What was the decisive argument?
A decisive moment leaves nothing still open.
She was decisive under pressure and calm afterwards.
Decisive settles the matter; divisive splits it.

decomposer.childMeaning: A living thing that breaks down dead material.
practiceSentences: Fungi are the forest's most important decomposers.
What would happen without decomposers?
A decomposer returns nutrients to the soil.
Decomposers are the last link, and also the first.
Bacteria and fungi are the two great groups of decomposers.

deduce.childMeaning: To work something out from the evidence you already have.
practiceSentences: From the muddy footprints we can deduce which way he went.
What can you deduce from the opening paragraph?
A reader deduces the ending long before it arrives.
She deduced the answer without being told any of it.
To deduce is to reason, not to guess.

denotation.childMeaning: The plain dictionary meaning of a word.
practiceSentences: The denotation of home is the place where you live.
What is the denotation of this word?
Denotation is what the dictionary says; connotation is what it suggests.
Two words can share a denotation and feel quite different.
Denotation is fixed; connotation shifts with time and place.

density.childMeaning: How much mass is packed into a given space.
density.repitchedFrom: grade 5 unit 2: 'How much mass a substance has for its size.' - and this grade inherited it WORD FOR WORD with all five sentences, so a learner who completed Grade 5 would meet an identical card. It is one of two words the supplied list repeats from Grades 1-5, with `protagonist` in unit 1. Repitched to what Grade 6 adds: density as the reason things float, sink and layer, and the population sense this unit's geography needs.
practiceSentences: Oil floats because its density is lower than water's.
What is the population density of this district?
Warm air rises because heating lowers its density.
Density explains why the layers in the jar never mix.
Density is mass divided by volume, and nothing else.

dependency.childMeaning: The state of relying on something else.
practiceSentences: The valley's dependency on one river is a risk.
What dependency does this design have?
A dependency you cannot see is the dangerous kind.
Their dependency on imported fuel rose every year.
Dependency is the condition; dependence is the same idea.

dependent.childMeaning: Relying on something or someone else.
practiceSentences: The harvest is dependent on the March rains.
Is the whole plan dependent on one supplier?
A town dependent on a single crop has no cushion.
She was financially dependent until the shop broke even.
Dependent with an e is the adjective; a dependant is a person.

descending.childMeaning: Going down, or arranged from largest to smallest.
practiceSentences: Sort the results in descending order of size.
Is this table ascending or descending?
Descending order puts the largest value first.
The aeroplane was descending towards the coast.
Descending starts at the top and works down.

descriptive.childMeaning: Giving a clear picture of what something is like.
practiceSentences: Her descriptive writing put us on the mountainside.
What descriptive detail would help here?
Descriptive writing shows; explanatory writing tells.
The report was descriptive but drew no conclusion.
Descriptive keeps the i of describe as an e.
The development of the delta took ten thousand years.
What development would you expect next?
Development is slow, and then it is sudden.
The town's development followed the road exactly.
Development also means a plot of new buildings.

devise.childMeaning: To think out and plan something new.
practiceSentences: They set out to devise a cheaper way to pump water.
How would you devise a test for this?
To devise is to invent the method, not just the idea.
She devised a system that needed no electricity.
Devise is the verb; a device is what it produces.

dialect.childMeaning: A form of a language spoken in one area or by one group.
dialect.note: The inherited meaning began lowercase and ended without a full stop - one of four in this grade's draft that arrive that way, with persistent (u2) and transition (u8).
practiceSentences: Every region of the coast has its own dialect.
Which dialect is spoken in your grandmother's town?
A dialect is a way of speaking, not a mistake.
The story is written in dialect, so read it aloud.
A dialect has its own words and its own grammar.

diction.childMeaning: A writer's or speaker's choice of words.
practiceSentences: The poet's diction is plain and very exact.
How would you describe the diction of this speech?
Diction changes the mood more than the plot does.
Formal diction suits a report and not a fable.
Amara noticed the diction shift the moment the elder spoke.

difference.childMeaning: A way in which two things are not the same.
difference.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'A difference is a change or a way that...' - restating its own headword, and joining two ideas with `or` where the card needs one.
difference.note: The set held ONE sentence: 'This includes knowing the difference between needs and wants.' - it opens on a `This` that refers to nothing the card shows.
practiceSentences: The difference between the two reports is their evidence.
What difference does the extra paragraph make?
A small difference in wording can change the whole meaning.
She explained the difference between a fact and a claim.
Difference keeps the e of differ before the ending.

differentiate.childMeaning: To see or show the difference between two things.
practiceSentences: Can you differentiate a crocodile from an alligator?
How do you differentiate these two footprints?
Size alone will not differentiate the male from the female.
She learned to differentiate the calls by ear.
To differentiate is to name the difference, not just feel it.

diffusion.childMeaning: The spreading of a substance from where there is more to where there is less.
practiceSentences: Oxygen reaches the blood by diffusion.
How does diffusion move a scent across a room?
Diffusion needs no pump and no energy.
Diffusion stops when the amounts even out.
A drop of ink spreading through water is diffusion.

dilation.childMeaning: Making a shape larger or smaller while keeping its proportions.
practiceSentences: A dilation changes the size and not the shape.
What scale factor does this dilation use?
After a dilation the two shapes are similar, not congruent.
She drew the dilation from a centre point on the grid.
Dilation also means the widening of the pupil in an eye.

diplomacy.childMeaning: The managing of relations between countries by discussion.
practiceSentences: Diplomacy settled the dispute without a shot.
What does diplomacy achieve that force cannot?
Diplomacy works slowly and is noticed only when it fails.
Years of diplomacy produced a single page of agreement.
Diplomacy also means handling people tactfully.

disastrous.childMeaning: Causing very great harm or damage.
practiceSentences: Clearing the forest had disastrous effects on the river.
Why was that season so disastrous for the herd?
A disastrous drought can empty a valley in months.
Introducing one new species proved disastrous for the rest.
Disastrous keeps the o of disaster and loses the e.

discursive.childMeaning: Discussing a subject from several sides rather than arguing one.
practiceSentences: A discursive essay weighs both sides before deciding.
Is this piece discursive or persuasive?
A discursive text presents the strongest case for each view.
She chose a discursive form because the evidence was mixed.
Discursive explores; argumentative advocates.

distribution.note: Sentences 2 and 4 were the same sentence twice - 'The fair distribution of food ensured every family at the harvest gathering was fed.' beside 'Fair distribution of food after the storm meant that every hungry family received an equal portion.' One frame, one card.
practiceSentences: Careful distribution meant that the last lorry of rice reached even the most distant village.
The fair distribution of food ensured every family at the gathering was fed.
Why does the uneven distribution of wealth cause problems in so many societies?
Distribution is as difficult as production, and is planned for less.
I helped organise the distribution of books so no classroom was left without any.

documentary.childMeaning: A film or programme about real people and real events.
documentary.note: The inherited set held two sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: Unlike a drama, a documentary does not invent characters.
What makes a documentary trustworthy?
A documentary tells a true story about real people and places.
The documentary followed one family for three years.
A documentary still chooses what to show, which is a kind of argument.

domain.childMeaning: The name that identifies a website, or an area of knowledge.
practiceSentences: The school registered its own domain last year.
Which domain does this address belong to?
A domain name points to a computer somewhere.
Ancient history is not her domain.
A domain ending in .org tells you very little by itself.

dynamic.childMeaning: Always changing or full of energy and movement.
practiceSentences: A river delta is a dynamic landscape.
How dynamic is this population from year to year?
A dynamic system settles into no single state.
The herd's dynamic movement follows the rain.
Dynamic is the opposite of static.

embryo.childMeaning: A living thing in the earliest stage of its development.
practiceSentences: The embryo grows from a single fertilised cell.
How long does the embryo stage last?
An embryo is protected inside the seed or the body.
The embryo of a bean sits between the two halves.
Every large animal began as an embryo too small to see.
The appeal used emotive language throughout.
Which emotive word is doing the most work here?
Emotive writing moves a reader before it convinces them.
She replaced the emotive words with plain ones and the case grew stronger.
Emotive is not the same as dishonest, but it is worth noticing.

enjoyment.childMeaning: The pleasure you get from doing something.
enjoyment.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Enjoyment is the feeling of pleasure...' - restating its own headword.
practiceSentences: Reading for enjoyment is not the same as reading for a test.
What brings you the most enjoyment?
Enjoyment of a film survives knowing how it ends.
The programme is made for enjoyment rather than instruction.
Enjoyment keeps the y of enjoy before the ending.

enquire.note: Sentence 4 named Idris, who is not in this grade's readings - one of the two strays the grade-wide check has been reporting since unit 6.
practiceSentences: If one step confuses you, enquire before you carry on with the rest.
Nora went to the school office to enquire about the missing library book.
Shall we enquire at the community centre about the times for the fair?
"I would like to enquire about the science competition," said Amara politely.
Yesterday I enquired at the bookshop whether the new comics had arrived.

enterprise.childMeaning: A business, or the willingness to start something difficult.
practiceSentences: The bakery began as a family enterprise.
What enterprise would you start with a small loan?
An enterprise needs a customer before it needs a logo.
Her enterprise in finding a supplier saved the shop.
Enterprise means the business, and also the nerve to begin it.

enzyme.childMeaning: A substance that speeds up a chemical change inside the body.
practiceSentences: An enzyme in saliva begins breaking down starch.
Which enzyme acts on protein in the stomach?
An enzyme speeds a reaction without being used up.
Enzymes stop working if they get too hot.
Each enzyme fits one job, like a key in a lock.

equality.childMeaning: The state of everyone having the same rights and opportunities.
equality.note: The inherited set held ONE sentence - '"We must shift towards equality," the leader had said.' - a quoted fragment in the past perfect, which belongs to a scene the card never shows.
practiceSentences: Equality before the law means the same rules for everyone.
Is equality of opportunity the same as equality of outcome?
Equality is a starting point, not a result.
The reform aimed at equality of pay for the same work.
Equality treats people the same; equity treats them as needed.

equipped.childMeaning: Supplied with what is needed for a task.
practiceSentences: The team arrived well equipped for a week in the bush.
Is the camp equipped for the rainy season?
A camel is equipped for heat in ways a horse is not.
They equipped every ranger with a radio.
Equipped doubles the p before the ending.
An ethical photographer asks before taking the picture.
Is it ethical to edit a documentary this heavily?
An ethical choice may cost you the better story.
The gallery published its ethical guidelines.
Ethical asks what is right; legal asks what is allowed.
ethical.childMeaning: To do with what is morally right and fair.
ethical.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

practiceSentences: Medical ethics decide what a doctor may not do.
What ethics should govern a company's advertising?
Ethics ask what is right, not what is allowed.
The council published a code of ethics for its officers.
Ethics is the study; a rule is one of its conclusions.
ethics.childMeaning: Ideas about right and wrong, and how people should act.
ethics.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

evident.childMeaning: Clear and easy to see or understand.
practiceSentences: Her skill is evident in every brushstroke.
Is the artist's intention evident from the title?
What is evident to one viewer may be invisible to another.
The influence of the earlier painter is evident throughout.
Evident means plain to see; evidence is what makes it so.

evidently.childMeaning: In a way that is clear from what can be seen.
practiceSentences: He was evidently exhausted by the final lap.
Is the ankle evidently swollen, or only sore?
Evidently the notice had never been read.
She had evidently practised the routine many times.
Evidently means the evidence shows it, not that somebody said so.

excitement.childMeaning: A strong feeling of eagerness about something happening.
practiceSentences: The excitement in the hall was impossible to miss.
What causes the excitement in this scene?
Excitement makes a poor guide to whether something is true.
Advertising manufactures excitement on purpose.
Excitement keeps the e of excite before the ending.

excretion.childMeaning: The removal of waste the body has produced.
practiceSentences: Excretion removes what the body cannot use.
Which organs are involved in excretion?
Excretion and digestion are not the same process.
Sweating is a form of excretion as well as cooling.
Without excretion, waste would build up and poison the body.

explicit.childMeaning: Stated openly and clearly, leaving nothing to be guessed.
practiceSentences: The instructions were explicit about the deadline.
Was the warning explicit or merely suggested?
An explicit rule saves an argument later.
She made her disagreement explicit rather than hinting.
Explicit is stated; implicit is understood.

export.childMeaning: To send goods to another country to be sold there.
practiceSentences: The country exports coffee and imports machinery.
What does this region export?
Exports earn the foreign money a country needs.
They began to export once the port was rebuilt.
An export leaves; an import arrives.

extraordinary.note: The inherited set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: Dina's talent for weaving was truly extraordinary.
Isn't it extraordinary how quickly she finished the whole cloth?
What an extraordinary sunset this is tonight, Amal!
The scientist made an extraordinary discovery after years of study.
An extraordinary claim needs extraordinary evidence.

extrapolate.childMeaning: To use what you know to estimate beyond it.
practiceSentences: From four years of data they extrapolate the fifth.
Can you extrapolate the trend to next year?
To extrapolate far beyond your evidence is to invent.
She extrapolated the cost from the first three months.
Extrapolate reaches past the data; interpolate fills a gap inside it.
The plan is feasible if the parts arrive on time.
Is a solar version feasible for a village?
Feasible asks whether it CAN be done, not whether it should be.
They rejected two designs and kept the feasible one.
A feasible idea is one you could start on Monday.
feasible.repitchedFrom: the grade 8 meaning was 'Possible to do easily or conveniently.' - which is not what feasible means. A feasible plan is one that CAN be done; it may be very hard. The word for easy is convenient. Flagged for re-pitch by the draft tool, and wrong as well as high-pitched.

fertilisation.childMeaning: The joining of a male and a female cell to begin new life.
practiceSentences: Fertilisation is the first step in reproduction.
Where does fertilisation take place in a flower?
After fertilisation the cell begins to divide.
Fertilisation in fish usually happens in the water.
Fertilisation also describes feeding soil for crops.

finance.childMeaning: The managing of money, or the money needed for something.
practiceSentences: The council could not find the finance for the bridge.
Who manages the finance for the co-operative?
Finance decides which good ideas actually happen.
She studied finance and returned to advise the village.
To finance something is to pay for it over time.

firewall.childMeaning: A system that blocks unwanted traffic reaching a network.
practiceSentences: The firewall blocked the connection before it reached us.
What does the firewall let through?
A firewall filters traffic; it does not remove a virus already inside.
The school's firewall blocks some sites the class needs.
A firewall was originally a real wall that stopped a fire spreading.

firmware.childMeaning: Software stored permanently inside a device.
practiceSentences: The printer's firmware controls how it feeds paper.
When was the firmware last updated?
Firmware sits between hardware and ordinary software.
A firmware update can add features to a device you already own.
Firmware is firm because it is not meant to change often.

footprint.childMeaning: The trace a person or activity leaves behind.
footprint.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'A mark left in the ground by a foot or a shoe' - the literal sense, on a card between streaming and bias in a unit about media. Here the word is the digital and environmental trace, which is the reading this grade needs; the mark in the ground is named in the fifth sentence.
practiceSentences: Everything you post adds to your digital footprint.
How large is this factory's carbon footprint?
A footprint is left whether you meant to leave it or not.
She checked her own footprint by searching her name.
A footprint is also the mark a shoe leaves in soft ground.

foreshadowing.childMeaning: A hint early in a story about what will happen later.
practiceSentences: The storm on page one is foreshadowing.
Where does the foreshadowing begin?
Foreshadowing makes an ending feel earned rather than sudden.
You often notice the foreshadowing only on a second reading.
Good foreshadowing hints without giving anything away.

formula.childMeaning: A rule written in symbols showing how quantities relate.
practiceSentences: The formula for the area of a rectangle is length times width.
Which formula would you use here?
A formula works for every case, not just this one.
She substituted the numbers into the formula.
The plural of formula is formulae, or formulas.

fragile.note: All five inherited sentences were about MONEY - family finances, a small business, savings, a buyer and a seller - in a unit about wildlife. Only the last mentioned the natural world at all. Rewritten to this unit; the money sentences belong to unit 5, which teaches its own words for that.
practiceSentences: A coral reef is beautiful and extremely fragile.
Why is this habitat so fragile after a dry season?
A fragile ecosystem recovers slowly, if it recovers at all.
The eggs are fragile, so the rangers move nobody near them.
Fragile does not mean unimportant; it means easily lost.

fuel.childMeaning: A substance burned to release energy.
practiceSentences: Wood was the only fuel available in the valley.
Which fuel gives the most heat for its weight?
A fuel stores energy that burning releases.
The engine ran until the fuel was spent.
Fuel is also what keeps an argument going.

gene.childMeaning: A section of a chromosome that decides one inherited feature.
practiceSentences: A gene decides whether the seed grows tall or short.
Which gene controls the colour of the coat?
One gene can be carried without ever being shown.
Genes are passed on whole, not blended.
A gene is an instruction; the animal is the result.

generalise.childMeaning: To draw a wide conclusion from a small number of cases.
practiceSentences: It is unwise to generalise from one example.
Why do people generalise so quickly?
A fable invites you to generalise from one animal to many.
She refused to generalise about a whole town.
To generalise well you need more than two cases.

global.childMeaning: Affecting or covering the whole world.
practiceSentences: Migration routes are a global phenomenon.
What global change threatens this species?
A global problem needs more than a local answer.
The survey collected global data over ten years.
Global means worldwide, not merely widespread.

gradient.childMeaning: How steeply a line or a slope rises or falls.
practiceSentences: The road's gradient is one in ten.
What is the gradient of this line?
A gradient of zero is flat.
The river slows where the gradient eases.
Gradient is the rise divided by the distance across.

grammatical.childMeaning: Following the rules of grammar, or to do with grammar.
practiceSentences: The sentence is grammatical but very hard to read.
Is this construction grammatical in written English?
A grammatical sentence can still say nothing at all.
She marked every grammatical error in the transcript.
Grammatical describes the rules; grammar is the rules themselves.

graphics.childMeaning: Pictures and designs produced on a computer.
practiceSentences: The graphics carry more of the argument than the text does.
What graphics would make this data clearer?
Good graphics answer a question; decoration does not.
She redrew the graphics so they worked in black and white.
Graphics takes a plural verb even for one image set.

happiness.childMeaning: The feeling of being glad and content.
happiness.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Happiness is the warm, glad feeling...' - restating its own headword.
practiceSentences: Advertising promises happiness and sells a product.
What does happiness look like in this film's ending?
Happiness is harder to photograph than excitement.
She wrote about happiness without once using the word.
Happiness changes the y of happy to an i.
Tourists who harass an animal change how it behaves.
Why do smaller birds harass a hawk?
Do not harass a nesting bird for a photograph.
The rangers stop visitors who harass the elephants.
Harass has one r and two s's, which trips most people.
Henceforth the reserve will be closed to vehicles.
Will the rule apply henceforth, or from next year?
The species was henceforth protected by law.
Henceforth all sightings must be recorded on the same form.
Henceforth looks forward; hitherto looks back.

hindrance.note: Inherited whole and kept; the set is varied, inside the cap and about designing something, which is this unit.
practiceSentences: The rain was a hindrance to our outdoor game.
Bulky packaging is a real hindrance when families try to carry groceries home by bicycle.
Is a lack of recycling bins the biggest hindrance to sorting waste at school?
"My broken wrist was a hindrance," admitted Sami, "but the team adjusted the prototype schedule."
I thought rules would be a hindrance to creativity, yet limits actually sharpened our design.
hindrance.childMeaning: Something that gets in the way of what you are doing.
hindrance.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

hormone.childMeaning: A chemical messenger the body makes to control how it works.
practiceSentences: A hormone travels through the blood to reach its target.
Which hormone controls how tall a person grows?
Hormones work slowly compared with nerve signals.
One hormone can affect several parts of the body at once.
The class labelled where each hormone is made.

hypothesise.childMeaning: To suggest an explanation that can then be tested.
practiceSentences: We hypothesise that the shorter route is also the slower one.
What would you hypothesise from these readings?
To hypothesise is to propose something you intend to test.
She hypothesised a cause and designed an experiment for it.
If you cannot test what you hypothesise, it is only an opinion.
hypothesise.note: Sentence 5 used `hypothesis`, the noun, on a card teaching the verb.

imagination.note: All five inherited sentences were about SPORT - an athlete picturing success, a coach at warm-ups, games for the team after training - in the unit about the arts. That is unit 2's subject, taught with unit 2's own words. Rewritten to this unit.
practiceSentences: A painter needs imagination and a great deal of patience.
Where does a writer's imagination come from?
Imagination is not the opposite of accuracy.

leisure.childMeaning: Time when you are free to do as you please.
