Refining is where most of the invention actually happens.
refine.childMeaning: To improve something by small, careful changes.
refine.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

reform.note: The inherited set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: The council promised to reform the unfair rules that had troubled the community for years.
Why is it sometimes difficult to reform a system that many people are used to?
"We must reform these laws," the leader argued, "to protect the rights of everyone."
I signed a petition urging the school to reform its outdated recycling policy.
To reform is to reshape what exists, not to replace it.

refugee.note: Inherited whole and kept - varied, inside the cap, and about this unit's subject.
practiceSentences: A refugee carries hope, even when the journey feels very long.
The refugee family opened a small shop in our town.
How can our school welcome a new refugee student?
"Every refugee deserves safety and kindness," said the teacher.
We collected warm blankets for refugee children last winter.

reinforce.childMeaning: To make something stronger, or to support a point with more evidence.
practiceSentences: Steel rods reinforce the concrete beam.
What evidence would reinforce this argument?
A second source reinforces the first, or it contradicts it.
She reinforced the corners of the box with tape.
To reinforce is to add strength to what is already there.
Transport here is relatively cheap.
Is the fee relatively high for this district?
Relatively few families own the land they farm.
The scheme was relatively simple to run.
Relatively always leaves a question: compared with what?

represent.note: Sentences 1 and 5 were the SAME sentence, differing only in punctuation: 'Each of you will represent a group, she explained carefully.' and '"Each of you will represent a group," she explained carefully.' An exact duplicate on one card, which the cross-card check would catch across two cards and cannot see within one.
practiceSentences: Each of you will represent a group at the final debate.
Who will represent the fishermen at the discussion?
A single juror cannot represent every opinion in the room.
On this map, one centimetre represents a whole kilometre.
To represent is to stand for something, or to stand in for somebody.

reproduction.childMeaning: The process by which living things produce young.
practiceSentences: Reproduction is one of the signs of a living thing.
How does reproduction differ between plants and animals?
Reproduction passes characteristics from parent to offspring.
Some plants manage reproduction without any seeds.
Reproduction also means making a copy of a picture.

resistance.childMeaning: A force that slows something down as it moves through air or water.
resistance.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'The act of standing firm against something, such as unfair rules or control.' - the POLITICAL sense, on a card sitting beside acceleration, kinetic and transfer. In a unit about sport and the body, resistance is the force a swimmer and a cyclist work against.
practiceSentences: A swimmer's cap reduces resistance in the water.
How does a cyclist lower air resistance?
Resistance grows as a moving object goes faster.
The parachute works by creating as much resistance as possible.
Resistance in a wire turns electrical energy into heat.

respectfulness.childMeaning: Treating other people and their views with proper regard.
practiceSentences: Respectfulness costs nothing and is remembered.
What does respectfulness look like in a disagreement?
Respectfulness does not require agreement.
Her respectfulness towards every visitor set the tone.
Respectfulness is shown in how you listen, not only how you speak.

rhombus.childMeaning: A parallelogram with all four sides the same length.
practiceSentences: A rhombus is a pushed-over square.
Is this shape a rhombus or a kite?
A rhombus has four equal sides and no right angles needed.
The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles.
A square is a rhombus that also has right angles.

rigid.childMeaning: Stiff and not able to bend, or unwilling to change.
practiceSentences: A rigid frame does not flex under load.
Is the rule rigid, or is there room to judge?
A rigid plan breaks where a flexible one bends.
The card was rigid enough to stand upright.
Rigid describes a material, and also an attitude.

robotics.childMeaning: The design and building of machines that can act on their own.
practiceSentences: Robotics brings together coding, electronics and engineering.
What can robotics do that a person cannot?
Robotics needs a sensor as much as it needs a motor.
The robotics club built an arm that sorts by colour.
Robotics is a field; a robot is one thing in it.

rotational.childMeaning: To do with turning around a fixed point.
practiceSentences: The shape has rotational symmetry of order four.
Does this pattern have rotational symmetry?
Rotational symmetry means it looks the same after a turn.
A wheel's rotational movement is what carries the cart.
Rotational is turning; translational is sliding.

sacrifice.note: The inherited set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: The volunteers made a real sacrifice, giving up their weekends to rebuild the flooded school.
What sacrifice would you make to help a cause you truly believe in?
"Every great change requires sacrifice," the teacher reminded the determined young activists.
I understood the meaning of sacrifice when my parents worked extra hours for my education.
A sacrifice costs the person making it, or it is not one.

sadness.note: Sentence 4 named Theo, who belongs to Grades 2 and 3 - the EIGHTH, and the fifteenth stray cast name across the two grades.
practiceSentences: Talking about sadness can help another person feel understood.
Sadness filled the class when the holidays ended.
How do you chase sadness away on hard days?
Amara said, "Talking to Mum makes my sadness smaller."
I felt sadness when my best friend was ill.

sample.note: The inherited set held ONE sentence - 'One sample glowed faintly blue.' - which explains nothing standing alone and belongs to an experiment the card never shows.
practiceSentences: A sample is a small part chosen to stand for the whole.
How large a sample would you need to trust the result?
A sample chosen carelessly tells you about nobody.
They tested a sample of grain from every sack.
A census counts everyone; a sample counts a few and reasons from them.

satire.childMeaning: Writing that mocks something in order to criticise it.
practiceSentences: The cartoon is satire, not simple insult.
What is this satire actually attacking?
Satire uses humour to make a serious point.
The play was banned because its satire was too accurate.
Satire laughs at power; comedy may laugh at anything.

scrutinise.childMeaning: To examine something very closely and carefully.
practiceSentences: Scrutinise the photograph before naming the species.
Why scrutinise a result you already expected?
A scientist must scrutinise the method as well as the answer.
They scrutinised every entry in the field notebook.
To scrutinise is to look harder than seems necessary.

sector.childMeaning: One part of a country's economy or activity.
practiceSentences: The farming sector employs most people here.
Which sector is growing fastest?
A country that depends on one sector is fragile.
The public sector is paid for out of taxation.
Sector also means a part of a circle.

sediment.childMeaning: Material that settles at the bottom of a liquid.
practiceSentences: Sediment settles where the river slows down.
What sediment did the flood leave behind?
Layers of sediment record thousands of years.
Sediment buries the remains that later become fossils.
Stir the bottle and the sediment lifts again.

self-awareness.childMeaning: Understanding your own feelings, strengths and limits.
practiceSentences: Self-awareness helps an athlete know when to rest.
How would you describe your own self-awareness?
Self-awareness means noticing a mood before it becomes a mistake.
Dina showed self-awareness by admitting she had rushed.
Self-awareness is harder than being aware of everybody else.

self-discipline.childMeaning: Making yourself do what you planned, even when you would rather not.
practiceSentences: Training every morning takes real self-discipline.
Where does self-discipline come from?
Self-discipline is a habit long before it is a feeling.
Amal's self-discipline showed in her steady improvement.
Self-discipline is choosing later over now.

simulation.childMeaning: A model that copies how something real behaves, so it can be studied.
practiceSentences: A simulation lets you crash the bridge without building it.
How accurate is this simulation?
A simulation is only as good as what was put into it.
Pilots train on a simulation before they fly.
A simulation predicts; it does not prove.

sincere.note: Sentence 1 named Teacher Yasmin, who belongs to Grade 5 and is not in this grade's readings.
practiceSentences: The quiet paper was the most sincere one in the pile.
A sincere apology comes from the heart.
Was his thank-you sincere and true?
Grandma said, "A sincere friend tells you the truth."
I wrote a sincere note to thank my teacher.

solvent.childMeaning: A liquid that dissolves another substance.
practiceSentences: Water is the solvent in almost every living cell.
Which solvent will dissolve this stain?
A solvent does the dissolving; the solute is dissolved.
Warming the solvent makes it work faster.
Water is called the universal solvent for good reason.

sourcebook.childMeaning: A book that collects original documents on one subject.
practiceSentences: The sourcebook prints the letters in full.
Which sourcebook covers this period?
A sourcebook gives you the evidence rather than the conclusion.
She quoted from the sourcebook rather than the textbook.
A sourcebook collects sources; a textbook explains them.

sovereignty.childMeaning: A country's right to govern itself without outside control.
practiceSentences: Sovereignty means the decisions are made at home.
Does joining a treaty reduce sovereignty?
Sovereignty is claimed by a state and recognised by others.
The islands' sovereignty was disputed for a century.
Sovereignty is authority; independence is the condition of having it.

streaming.childMeaning: Playing video or music over the internet as it arrives, without downloading it first.
streaming.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'Flowing steadily and continuously, like a stream of liquid or light', with five sentences about water under a door, tears, sunlight and rain. On a card between pixel and footprint, in a unit about media, streaming is how a film reaches a screen. The water sense is real and belongs to a different unit entirely.
practiceSentences: Streaming plays the film as it arrives, so nothing is stored.
Why does streaming need more bandwidth than downloading a page?
Streaming stops the moment the connection does.
The match was watched by streaming in four countries at once.
Streaming also describes water flowing steadily, which is where the word came from.

subordinate.childMeaning: Depending on another part, as a subordinate clause depends on a main one.
subordinate.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'A person who has a lower position or rank than someone else' - the workplace sense, on a card between synthesis and modal in a unit about writing. Here subordinate is what a clause is when it cannot stand alone. The rank sense is named in the fifth sentence.
practiceSentences: A subordinate clause cannot stand as a sentence on its own.
Which part of this sentence is subordinate?
A subordinate clause usually opens with a word like although or because.
She joined the two ideas with a subordinate clause.
Subordinate also describes a person of lower rank.

substantial.note: Sentence 5 was 'But something inside her - small but substantial - told her to speak.' Lifted from a narrative: it opens with `But`, names a `her` the card never introduces, and uses the word figuratively where the other four use it of amounts.
practiceSentences: The library received a substantial donation that funded meals for many needy families.
How long would it take to save such a substantial amount from weekly pocket money?
"That's a substantial saving," Sami noted, "if we buy in bulk and share the cost."
I put a substantial part of my earnings aside before spending anything on myself.
Substantial means large enough to matter, not merely large.

subtle.childMeaning: Slight and not obvious, but there if you look carefully.
practiceSentences: There is a subtle difference between the two endings.
Was the change subtle enough to miss?
A subtle hint is easily overlooked on a first reading.
The fable makes its point in a subtle way.
Subtle is spelled with a b nobody says.

superior.childMeaning: Better than something else, or higher in rank.
practiceSentences: The second design proved superior in every test.
Which method is superior for this task?
A superior result deserves an explanation, not just applause.
She reported the fault to her superior.
Superior means better than something named, so name it.

sustainable.childMeaning: Able to continue for a long time without using everything up.
practiceSentences: Sustainable fishing leaves enough behind to breed.
Is this way of farming sustainable?
A sustainable harvest takes the interest, not the capital.
The reserve was designed to be sustainable for a century.
Sustainable asks what happens in fifty years, not next season.

synthesis.childMeaning: The combining of several sources or ideas into one whole.
practiceSentences: A good conclusion is a synthesis, not a summary.
What synthesis do these three reports allow?
Synthesis puts sources into conversation with each other.
Her synthesis of the interviews produced one clear argument.
A summary shortens one source; a synthesis joins several.

tangent.childMeaning: A straight line that touches a curve at exactly one point.
practiceSentences: The tangent touches the circle and does not cross it.
Where does the tangent meet the curve?
A tangent meets a circle at one point only.
She drew a tangent to find the slope at that instant.
To go off on a tangent is to leave the subject suddenly.
Taxation pays for the roads and the clinics.
Is taxation fairer when the richest pay a larger share?
Taxation takes from everyone and spends on everyone.
The council explained where the taxation went.
Taxation is the system; a tax is one charge within it.
taxation.childMeaning: The system by which a government collects money from people.
taxation.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

technical.childMeaning: To do with the practical details of how something works.
practiceSentences: The technical drawing shows every measurement.
What technical problem stopped the first model?
A technical explanation is not the same as a clear one.
She read the technical manual twice before starting.
Technical detail belongs in an appendix, not an introduction.

tectonic.childMeaning: To do with the huge plates that make up the Earth's surface.
practiceSentences: Tectonic plates move a few centimetres each year.
Which tectonic boundary runs beneath this valley?
Tectonic movement built every mountain range on Earth.
An earthquake happens where two tectonic plates slip.
A tectonic shift also means a very large change in anything.

tessellation.childMeaning: A pattern of shapes that fits together with no gaps.
practiceSentences: The floor tiles form a perfect tessellation.
Which shapes make a tessellation on their own?
A tessellation leaves no gaps and no overlaps.
A hexagon tessellation is why a honeycomb is strong.
A circle cannot make a tessellation, however it is arranged.
tessellation.note: Sentence 4 used `tessellate`, the verb, on a card teaching the noun.

theoretically.childMeaning: According to the idea, though perhaps not in practice.
practiceSentences: Theoretically the fund is open to everyone.
Is that theoretically possible or actually possible?
Theoretically the two routes cost the same.
The scheme theoretically pays for itself within a year.
Theoretically signals that reality has not been consulted yet.

theorise.childMeaning: To form an idea that explains a set of facts.
practiceSentences: Historians theorise about why the settlement was abandoned.
What would you theorise from this evidence?
To theorise before gathering evidence is to guess.
She theorised that the two events were connected.
To theorise is to explain many facts; to hypothesise is to test one.
theorise.note: Sentence 5 used `theory`, the noun, on a card teaching the verb.

thereafter.childMeaning: After that time; from then on.
practiceSentences: The paper appeared weekly thereafter.
Did the policy change thereafter?
Thereafter every article carried its author's name.
The first edition sold out, and thereafter reprints followed.
Thereafter looks forward from a point already named.

therein.childMeaning: In that place, or in that particular thing.
practiceSentences: The archive and the letters therein are open to readers.
What lies therein that we have not read?
Therein lies the difficulty with the whole plan.
She cited the catalogue and the essay therein.
Therein points inside something already named.
Thermal energy moves from hot to cold, always.
What thermal protection does the roof need?
A thermal image shows where a building leaks heat.
Birds ride a thermal to gain height without flapping.
Thermal comes from the Greek word for heat.

thus.childMeaning: For that reason; in this way.
practiceSentences: The road flooded; thus the market was cancelled.
Is the conclusion thus proved, or only suggested?
Thus the two departments came to share a budget.
She missed the deadline and thus lost the contract.
Thus is a formal way of saying "so", and takes a semicolon before it.
thus.note: Quoted a word in BACKTICKS - code notation on a learner card.

tourism.note: Inherited whole and kept - varied, inside the cap, and about this unit's subject.
practiceSentences: Tourism brings buses full of visitors to our seaside town.
Tourism gives many families in our town their jobs.
How does tourism help protect the old fort?
"Tourism grows when we keep our beaches clean," said the mayor.
My uncle works in tourism, guiding visitors around the city.
You can trace the motif back to the opening page.
Can you trace this saying to its original teller?
Historians trace the custom to a single village.
She traced the argument through every paragraph.
Trace the idea backwards and you find its source.
trace.childMeaning: To follow something back to where it started.
trace.repitchedFrom: the meaning came straight from grade 8, two grades above this one, and the draft tool had been flagging it as `re-pitch meaning` all along.

practiceSentences: The transcript records every word, including the pauses.
Where is the transcript of that interview?
A transcript is exact; a summary is not.
She checked the quotation against the transcript.
A transcript captures the words and loses the tone.

transfer.childMeaning: To move something from one place, person or form to another.
practiceSentences: Energy transfers from the muscles to the ball.
How does heat transfer through a metal spoon?
The player asked for a transfer to another club.
Transfer the reading into the table before you leave.
Energy is never lost, only transferred.

transition.childMeaning: A change from one state or stage to another.
transition.note: The inherited meaning began lowercase and ended without a full stop - the LAST of the four in this grade's draft that arrived that way, after dialect and credible in unit 1 and persistent in unit 2.
practiceSentences: The transition from print to screen took twenty years.
What manages the transition between these two paragraphs?
A transition should carry the reader, not jolt them.
The film's transition to the next scene is deliberately abrupt.
A transition is the moving between; a change is the result.

translation.childMeaning: Sliding a shape to a new position without turning or resizing it.
translation.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'A translation is a piece of writing or speech changed from one language into another' - the LANGUAGE sense, restating its own headword, and holding only four sentences. On a card between triangular and rotational, translation is one of the three ways a shape can be moved. The language sense is named in the fifth sentence, since a Grade 6 learner meets both.
practiceSentences: A translation slides the shape without turning it.
How far is this translation, and in which direction?
A translation changes position and nothing else.
She described the translation as three right and two up.
Translation also means putting words into another language.

trapezium.childMeaning: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides.
practiceSentences: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides.
Which side of this trapezium is the longer parallel one?
A trapezium's area uses the average of the two parallel sides.
The dam's cross-section is a trapezium.
In British usage a trapezium has one parallel pair.

treaty.childMeaning: A formal written agreement between countries.
practiceSentences: The treaty ended forty years of dispute.
Which countries signed the treaty?
A treaty binds the country, not the government that signed it.
The treaty set the border along the river.
A treaty is written down; an understanding may not be.

tremendous.note: The inherited set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: What a tremendous storm that was last night!
Sami showed tremendous courage when he rescued the kitten.
Building the new bridge required a tremendous amount of effort.
Wasn't the noise from the concert absolutely tremendous?
Tremendous once meant frightening, and still carries some of that.

triangular.childMeaning: Shaped like a triangle, or having three sides.
practiceSentences: The roof panel is triangular.
Which triangular shape is the strongest?
A triangular frame does not fold the way a square one does.
She cut the cloth into triangular pieces.
Triangular describes the shape; a triangle is the shape itself.

troubleshoot.childMeaning: To find out what is going wrong and put it right.
practiceSentences: Troubleshoot the power supply before blaming the software.
How would you troubleshoot a machine that will not start?
To troubleshoot is to work from the simplest cause upwards.
She troubleshoots by removing one part at a time.
Troubleshooting is a method, not a talent.

undoubtedly.childMeaning: Certainly, with no room for doubt.
practiceSentences: The reform undoubtedly helped the poorest families.
Is that undoubtedly true, or merely likely?
Undoubtedly the scheme cost more than was promised.
She is undoubtedly the best candidate for the post.
Undoubtedly claims certainty, so it should be used sparingly.

utilise.childMeaning: To make practical use of something.
practiceSentences: The design utilises heat that would otherwise be wasted.
What materials could we utilise instead?
To utilise is to put to use, often something already there.
They utilised old bicycle parts in the frame.
Utilise usually means use, and use is usually the better word.
A frog is a vertebrate and a beetle is not.
Which vertebrates live in this river?
Every vertebrate has an internal skeleton.
Fish were the first vertebrates to appear.
Vertebrates are a small share of all animal species.

vitamin.childMeaning: A nutrient the body needs in small amounts to stay healthy.
practiceSentences: Oranges are rich in vitamin C.
Which vitamin does sunlight help the body make?
A vitamin is needed in tiny amounts, but needed all the same.
Vitamins are lost when vegetables are boiled too long.
No single vitamin can replace a varied diet.
A tired player is vulnerable to injury.
Who is most vulnerable in very hot weather?
An unguarded goal is vulnerable from any angle.
She admitted feeling vulnerable before her first race.
Being vulnerable is a condition, not a weakness.

wavelength.childMeaning: The distance between one wave's peak and the next.
practiceSentences: Red light has a longer wavelength than blue.
What wavelength does this station broadcast on?
A shorter wavelength carries more energy.
The wavelength of a sea wave can be measured from a pier.
Being on the same wavelength means understanding each other.

whichever.childMeaning: Any one of the choices, no matter which.
whichever.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Whichever means any one of the choices...' - restating its own headword.
practiceSentences: Take whichever route is shorter today.
Whichever shape you choose, measure it twice.
Whichever answer you give, show your working.
She would be pleased with whichever result came first.
Whichever narrows a choice; whatever leaves it open.

whom.childMeaning: The form of "who" used when the person is the object.
whom.note: The inherited set held ONE sentence - 'A food chain shows who eats whom.' - which is also unit 3's sentence for `chain`. One line serving two cards in two different units, which is the fault the cross-card check exists to find. The meaning first quoted `who` in BACKTICKS - written one unit after the rule against them was added, and caught by it on its first outing.
practiceSentences: To whom should the report be addressed?
Whom did the committee choose in the end?
The engineer whom they consulted had built three dams.
Ask for whom the measurement was taken.
Use whom after a preposition: to whom, for whom, with whom.

workforce.childMeaning: All the people who work for an employer or in a country.
practiceSentences: The factory's workforce doubled in two years.
How large is the workforce in this district?
A skilled workforce attracts the businesses that need it.
Half the workforce is under thirty.
Workforce counts the people; labour counts the work.
